name: subba – AI Receptionist, Chatbot & Online Booking
author: Roland

sections.description:
subba is the AI receptionist and booking system for local businesses. It answers your website enquiries in seconds, in your voice, and books customers straight into your diary, so you stop losing work to missed messages and slow replies. This plugin connects your WordPress site to your subba account in a couple of clicks.

It adds four things to your site:

  • AI chat widget – a chat bubble in the corner that answers questions about your services, hours and prices, captures the enquiry, and can take a booking. Powered by your subba account, so it always knows your real, up-to-date information.
  • Online booking embed – a [subba_booking] shortcode drops your booking widget onto any page or post. Customers pick a service and time and book themselves in, 24/7. The embed resizes itself to fit your page.
  • Online ordering embed – for restaurants, cafes and takeaways, a [subba_order] shortcode puts your menu and online ordering on any page: orders at the table, for collection or for delivery, with card payments through your own Stripe account. Guests come back to the same page after paying, and adding ?table= and a table’s code to the page’s link opens that table’s menu, for the QR codes on your tables.
  • Contact form forwarding – submissions from your existing forms are sent to subba automatically, so every enquiry lands in one inbox and gets an instant reply. Works with Contact Form 7, Gravity Forms, WPForms and Ninja Forms out of the box, no reconfiguration.

Why business owners use subba

  • Never miss another enquiry – the AI replies day and night, even when you are on a job or closed.
  • Turn website visitors into booked appointments, not unanswered messages.
  • Keep chat, forms and bookings in one place instead of scattered across email, socials and voicemail.
  • Set it up in minutes on any WordPress theme; no code required.

Great for salons, barbers, restaurants, cafes and takeaways, clinics, dentists, trades and electricians, gyms and studios, cleaners, garages, and any local business that books appointments or takes enquiries.

You need a subba account at subba.pro to use this plugin, and new accounts get their first 30 days free. Click Connect with subba to sign up or sign in, approve, and the plugin sets itself up.

External services

This plugin connects your site to subba, a service operated by Polarize Ltd, so the chat, booking and enquiry features can work. It is required for the plugin to function, and nothing is sent until you connect or configure it. Here is exactly what is sent, and when:

  1. Chat widget (api.subba.pro). When the chat widget is enabled, each page that shows it loads a small launcher script from https://api.subba.pro/f/<your form id>/chat.js and opens the chat in a subba-hosted frame. If a visitor uses the chat, the messages they type and any contact details they choose to give (such as name, email or phone) are sent to subba to generate a reply and log the enquiry. Nothing is sent for visitors who do not open the chat.
  2. Booking embed (book.subba.pro). On any page that uses the [subba_booking] shortcode, your booking widget is embedded from https://book.subba.pro/b/<your booking handle>. Details a visitor enters to make a booking (such as name, email, phone, chosen service and time) are sent to subba to create the booking.
  3. Ordering embed (book.subba.pro). On any page that uses the [subba_order] shortcode, a script is loaded from https://book.subba.pro/b/<your booking handle>/order.js and your order page is embedded from https://book.subba.pro. The script passes the address of that page to subba, so guests can be sent back to it after paying. Details a guest enters to order (such as name, email, number of people, special requests and the dishes chosen) are sent to subba to place the order; card payments are taken by Stripe on your own Stripe account.
  4. Form forwarding (api.subba.pro). When form forwarding is enabled, a submission from a supported form plugin is sent to https://api.subba.pro/f/<your form id> so subba can answer and log it. The data sent is the submitter’s name, email address and message, plus a “source” label of “wordpress”. Submissions are only forwarded while this option is switched on.
  5. Connecting (app.subba.pro and api.subba.pro). When you click Start free for 30 days, Get started with subba or Connect with subba, your browser goes to https://app.subba.pro with this site’s address and name, the address to come back to, and two random values that secure the connection. After you sign up or sign in and approve, this site’s server sends subba a one-time code and a secret value at https://api.subba.pro/connect/token, and receives your Form ID, booking handle and business name, which are saved in your WordPress settings. No password, key or token for your subba account is stored in WordPress. Nothing is sent unless you click one of these buttons.

By enabling these features you agree to subba’s terms and privacy policy:

  • Terms of service: https://subba.pro/terms
  • Privacy policy: https://subba.pro/privacy
sections.installation:
1. Install the plugin: in your WordPress admin go to Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin, choose subba.zip, then Install Now. Or upload the subba folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Click Activate. A welcome screen opens once: choose Start free for 30 days if you are new to subba, Get started with subba if you already have an account, or Open settings.
  3. subba opens: sign up or sign in, then approve the connection. You come back to WordPress already connected. (You can also click Connect with subba in Settings > subba at any time.)
  4. Prefer to set it up by hand? In Settings > subba, paste your chat widget code (under Settings > AI receptionist in your subba dashboard) and your booking link (under Settings > Booking). The plugin picks out your Form ID and booking handle.
  5. To show your booking widget on a page, add the shortcode [subba_booking] to any page or post.
  6. Restaurants, cafes and takeaways: to put your menu and online ordering on a page, add the shortcode [subba_order].
sections.faq:
Do I need a subba account?

Yes. subba does the AI answering, booking and enquiry logging; this plugin connects your WordPress site to it. Click Connect with subba in Settings > subba to create an account or sign in. New accounts get their first 30 days free.

Is connecting safe?

Yes. It works like signing in with Google: you approve the connection on subba, and WordPress receives only your Form ID and booking handle, which are public anyway (they appear in your site’s page source). No password, key or token for your subba account is stored in WordPress, and you can disconnect at any time in Settings > subba.

Where do I find my Form ID and booking handle?

In your subba dashboard: your chat widget code is under Settings > AI receptionist, and your booking link is under Settings > Booking. Paste either straight into Settings > subba and the plugin picks out the Form ID (the code after /f/) and the booking handle (the short name after /b/, for example zen-yoga).

Which contact form plugins are supported?

Contact Form 7, Gravity Forms, WPForms and Ninja Forms are forwarded automatically with no extra setup. Any other form still works through the chat widget, which works on every page.

Will it slow down my site?

No. The chat script is loaded in the footer and the booking widget loads in its own frame, so your pages render normally. Form submissions are forwarded in the background and never hold up the visitor.

What data is sent to subba, and is it private?

Only what is needed for each feature to work: chat messages and any contact details a visitor provides, booking details when someone books, and the name, email and message from a forwarded form submission. See the “External services” section above and subba’s privacy policy for the full detail.

Does it work with any theme?

Yes. The chat bubble and the booking and ordering embeds work with any standard WordPress theme, and the settings live under Settings > subba.

How do I remove it?

Deactivate and delete the plugin from the Plugins screen. Once removed, the chat widget, the booking and ordering embeds and form forwarding stop, and no further data is sent to subba.
sections.changelog:
1.0.5

  • A page for food and another for drinks: tabs shows only some of your menu’s tabs, under your own title, and the guest’s order follows them from page to page: [subba_order tabs="Wine, Gin" title="Drinks menu"].
  • choices="shown" puts each dish’s choices on its card (sizes, extras, a pizza built in steps), and checkout="page" gives the guest’s details a checkout page of their own. Both can also be set in your subba dashboard.

1.0.4

  • Online ordering for restaurants, cafes and takeaways: the [subba_order] shortcode puts your menu and ordering on any page. Guests order at the table or for collection or delivery, pay by card through your own Stripe account, and come back to the same page afterwards with their order confirmation.
  • Add ?table= and a table’s code to the page’s link to open that table’s menu, for the QR codes on your tables.
  • Pick the look in the shortcode, as in your subba dashboard: [subba_order style="night" layout="grid"].

1.0.3

  • Connect with subba: link this site to your subba account in one click. Sign up or sign in, approve, and the plugin fills in its own settings. No codes to copy, and no password or key stored in WordPress.
  • A welcome screen when you activate the plugin: start free for 30 days, get started with an account you already have, or open the settings. It shows once, and you can close it at any time.
  • Settings > subba also takes your chat widget code and booking link exactly as copied from your subba dashboard, if you prefer to paste them.
  • A Get started link (or, once connected, a link to your subba dashboard) on the Plugins screen, and a Disconnect button in the settings.
  • The booking embed now reports each step (subba_booking_view through subba_booking_complete) to your site’s Google Analytics 4, Google Tag Manager, Plausible or Matomo, with no setup. Events never include customer details.

1.0.2

  • Added the official subba plugin icon and banner on the WordPress.org listing.
  • Housekeeping release; no changes to plugin functionality.

1.0.1

  • Updated the plugin listing metadata (readme contributors).

1.0.0

  • Initial release.
  • AI chat widget, enabled site-wide from the settings screen.
  • [subba_booking] shortcode that embeds your booking widget and auto-resizes to fit the page.
  • Automatic enquiry forwarding for Contact Form 7, Gravity Forms, WPForms and Ninja Forms.
